newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes firmer as futures rally, Tapis up.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes firmer as futures rally, Tapis up.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Wednesday as futures prices firmed in the wake of U.S. stock data.
The Brent/Dubai November spread came in to $1.95/$2.05 from $2.08/$2.20 but was stretching back out again as London opened owing to the firmer tone of the Brent futures market.
November Brent rose 39 cents to $22.10 on SIMEX and London maintained the firmer tone at its opening.
But Dubai intermonth spreads were mostly steady, although offers came down slightly to tighten the bid/offer. Nov/Dec was quoted at 35/40 from 37/43 and Dec/Jan was at 35/40 from 35/42.
Paper Tapis started the day flat at $21.75/$21.95 for October before firming amid higher futures prices to $21.90/$22.20.
In wet trades, a November Umm Shaiff changed hands at ADNOC plus 30 cents between a European major and a Japanese trader.
A cargo of Dai Hung was sold in a tender to U.S. major Exxon at APPI Tapis quotes plus 21 cents. Some traders said China may have bought some Dai Hung also.
China was putting together a 1.3 million barrel cargo of Minas made up by end September barrels and early loading October barrels, traders said.
The overall prices range for the cargo was ICP less 5/10 cents to ICP flat, traders said.
China was expected to remain a buyer of crude to replace lost production from its 120,000 barrels-per-day Xijiang field which is still down after more than a week needing repairs.

Oman crude for October remained in the doldrums, although traders said they expected November levels to be flat to five cents down. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, Miho Yoshikawa, (+813 5473 3706)
